quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #7
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What should you do when you see a flashing yellow light?
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means there may be a hazard ahead. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: Why should drivers watch carefully for motorcycles, bicycles, and pedestrians?

options.text: They are hard to see on the road.
They follow different traffic laws than cars.
They do not have rearview mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are hard to see on the road.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles, bicycles, and pedestrians are smaller and harder to spot than cars. They may also move faster or have dimmer lights. Always stay alert for these smaller road users.

questions.question: What can you do to prevent rear-end collisions?

options.text: Check your mirrors and blind spots before you stop.
Release the gas pedal and let your car slow down before braking.

questions.explanation: To prevent rear-end collisions, avoid sudden stops. Before stopping, check your mirrors and blind spots. Release the gas pedal first to let your car slow down smoothly before you brake.

questions.question: What should you do when an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is near you?

options.text: Speed up to get away from it.
Stop your car and block its path.
Move out of the way and give it a clear path.
Signal to the vehicle when it is safe to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move out of the way and give it a clear path.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, move your car to the side of the road if it is safe. Give the emergency vehicle as much space as possible.

questions.question: Why is a leaky exhaust system dangerous?

options.text: It can poison you with carbon monoxide.
It makes the engine run poorly.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can poison you with carbon monoxide.
questions.explanation: The exhaust system removes dangerous fumes from your car. A leak lets harmful carbon monoxide gas into the passenger area. Fix any exhaust leaks right away.

questions.question: Two drivers arrive at the same time to a four-way stop. Who goes first?

options.text: One driver can drive without stopping.
One driver should honk to give up the right-of-way.

questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, if two cars arrive at the same time, the driver on your right has the right-of-way. Wait for them to go, then you may proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: Where is it not allowed to pass another vehicle?
questions.explanation: Never pass another vehicle on hills, curves, at intersections, or at railroad crossings. These areas are unsafe for passing.

questions.question: When can you drive on the left side of a two-lane road?

options.text: When passing at a railroad crossing.
In a safe passing zone while passing a car ahead of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: In a safe passing zone while passing a car ahead of you.
questions.explanation: You may only use the left lane to pass when it is safe and legal. Never pass at railroad crossings, on hills, or in curves where you cannot see oncoming traffic.

questions.question: When should you use your horn?

options.text: When a child is about to run into the street.

questions.correctAnswerText: When a child is about to run into the street.
questions.explanation: Use your horn to warn others when they may not see you. For example, honk if a child starts to run into the street in front of your car.

questions.question: If your turn signals do not work, what should you use to show you are turning?
questions.explanation: If your turn signals do not work, use hand signals to tell other drivers which way you are turning.

questions.question: When may you pass another vehicle?

options.text: On a curve or hill because few vehicles are coming.
By driving on the shoulder of the road.
If a solid yellow line is next to your lane and the passing lane is clear ahead.

questions.explanation: Do not pass on hills or curves. You cannot see oncoming traffic and may crash. Never pass by driving on the shoulder. You cannot pass over a solid yellow line.

questions.question: Do drivers have to yield to pedestrians who cross against the traffic light?
questions.explanation: You must always yield to pedestrians. Watch for pedestrians who may cross against the light by mistake.

questions.question: How should you enter a freeway?

options.text: Signal, yield to traffic, and match the speed of the traffic already on the freeway.
Signal and enter. Freeway traffic must yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, yield to traffic, and match the speed of the traffic already on the freeway.
questions.explanation: When merging onto a freeway, signal and match the speed of traffic already on the road. Always yield to other vehicles when entering a freeway.

questions.question: As alcohol builds up in your blood, what happens?

options.text: Your body breaks down alcohol faster.

questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reactions, makes you feel more confident (which is dangerous), and causes more driving errors.

questions.question: A driver entering interstate traffic from an entrance or acceleration ramp should:

options.text: Yield to drivers already on the interstate.
Assume other drivers will change lanes for them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to drivers already on the interstate.
questions.explanation: When entering an interstate from a ramp, yield to traffic already on the highway. Merge safely when there is an opening.

questions.question: When must you always use your signal?

options.text: When pulling into or out of a parking space.
When pulling into traffic from a parking area or alley.

questions.explanation: Use your turn signal whenever you move left or right. Signal when entering traffic from a parking space, changing lanes, or passing another vehicle.

questions.question: What is the most important thing to remember about speed and curves?

options.text: Drive at the speed limit as you enter the curve, then slow down at the sharpest part.
Slow down before you enter the curve.
Speed up gently before you enter the curve.
Drive at the speed limit before, during, and after the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before you enter the curve.
questions.explanation: Slow down before entering a curve. Your vehicle's momentum makes it hard to turn. Slowing down first helps you stay in control.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The traffic signal ahead is red.
The traffic signal ahead is broken.
The traffic signal ahead is green.
A traffic signal is coming up ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A traffic signal is coming up ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a traffic signal is at the next intersection.

questions.question: What commonly causes traffic accidents?

options.text: Driving too fast for the conditions

questions.explanation: Speeding causes many crashes. Not paying attention can cause you to hit other vehicles. Most rear-end collisions happen because drivers follow too closely.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign shows that the right lane will end ahead.

questions.question: How can you avoid making emergency stops while driving in traffic?

options.text: Honk your horn to alert other drivers.
Look ahead and stay a safe distance behind other cars.
Drive only in the right lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead and stay a safe distance behind other cars.
questions.explanation: A safe following distance gives you time to react to problems ahead without sudden braking. This prevents drivers behind you from crashing into your vehicle.

questions.question: If you reach an intersection where you want to turn but are not in the correct lane, you should:

options.text: Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.
Turn on your blinker and turn from your current lane.
Go to the next intersection and turn there.
Change lanes safely, then back up to return to the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go to the next intersection and turn there.
questions.explanation: Never make last-minute turns. If you are not in the correct lane to turn, drive to the next intersection and turn from the proper lane.

questions.question: If you are in an accident and someone is injured, you should:

options.text: Move the injured person away from the scene right away.
Always leave the injured person where they are.
Keep the injured person in place, keep them warm, and give first aid.
Stay away from the injured person.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the injured person in place, keep them warm, and give first aid.
questions.explanation: Do not move an injured person unless necessary. Moving them incorrectly can make minor injuries worse. Keep them warm until help arrives. If there is heavy bleeding, apply direct pressure to stop it.

questions.question: Distracted driving is:

options.text: Just as safe as normal driving.

questions.explanation: Distracted driving is extremely dangerous. It puts you, your passengers, pedestrians, cyclists, and other drivers at risk. Staying focused on driving helps prevent crashes.

questions.question: Who must yield when a driver is turning and a pedestrian is crossing without a traffic light?
questions.explanation: Drivers must yield to pedestrians crossing at any intersection without a traffic light, whether or not there is a crosswalk.
